recommendation.smallest_increment: Preserve recognized payload-free leading setup words before ContentStart in the existing source-context encode/controls path. recommendation.responsibility: Source-context encoding preserves renderer-state prefix bytes and speaker substitution at their original ordinal; it must not create a new parser or authoring framework. encode already owns copying/encoding, controls owns source grammar/readiness/complete validation; existing auditStreams and plan callers then reuse it. No new function is justified.
recommendation.do_not_silently_expand: Plain leading colour and existing explicit mixed-marker semantics are distinct. Keep colour/scale/icon/opaque domains held in the first setup increment unless an explicit source convention is separately bound. No planner layout, source fit, runtime semantics or registry status may be inferred from copying a prefix.
recommendation.why_not_all_leading_controls: Original plain encoder copies HL state verbatim; original mixed encoder filters leading HL then places EN markup. Current Go scanner counts leading HL in the EN marker sequence, and encode skips prefix HL/icon. Blindly copying them would change existing marker outputs and readiness diagnostics.

primary_source_contract.fact: Leading decoder loop recognizes at most one HDR and speaker plus setup/HL/pen0; stops for content/ICON/param8/duplicates. Main decoder still produces recognized tokens. HDR is not required at byte0; require_hdr is a separate source-reader restriction. setup4000..47ff and a800..afff are self-contained; nonzero pen families have no inline payload. Exact4800/b000/d800 have8Bpayload and remain separate.

jp_prologue boundary is first glyph/page/line/space/end, not merely decoder leading-loop length. Therefore ICON/param8 can be classified as prologue by this function even though they stop the decoder leading loop. This mismatch is material to the opaque bug.

encode_stream emits each prologue token word verbatim in source order, substitutes page0 EN speaker in place (or appends EN speaker if source lacked it), emits EN page/line structure, appends structural source final PAGE then END—even after explicit English final PAGE. It writes only word, not token.payload.

encode_entry_from_elf decodes original source and rejects setup/pen0/param8/icon/HL inside CONTENT (except separately reviewed HL wrapping); it does not reject those kinds in the computed prologue. The plain path rejects any {{...}} EN markup.

Markup-aware algorithms deliberately remove leading HL from filtered JP before encode_stream, so explicit EN markers can reposition colour without duplicated prefix. Original plain and mixed policy outputs must remain distinct.
